audit.why: 45.42% over 753 games with Tryndamere owning levels 4 onward is consistent, and the text is honest that Rumble's only edge is levels 2-3. No inflation to correct.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage is given a '110-second cooldown' in spikes[1] and again in wants.you[1]. The real cooldown is 120/100/80 — 110 is not the value at any rank.
audit.why: The entire level-6-onward plan in this matchup is 'commit only while Rage is down'. If the number a player counts to is wrong, every all-in timed off it is wrong, and the error is repeated in two places so it reads as verified.
audit.corrected: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1, 100s at rank 2, 80s at rank 3. The rank-1 window is a full two minutes — that is the real spike to play around.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanics are described backwards. (a) Mocking Shout (W) is presented as an unconditional slow that 'drops your movement speed, letting him out-chase you' — Riot's text slows only enemies with their backs turned to him; the unconditional part is an attack-damage reduction, which does nothing to an AP Rumble. (b) Tryndamere's healing is called 'passive fury regen' and 'his Q passive fury regen' in two places — Bloodlust's heal is an active cast on a 12s cooldown that consumes Fury; only the attack-damage ramp is passive.
audit.why: Point 4 is the key point and both errors change what the player does. If the slow only lands when you turn away, then walking into him with Flamespitter is strictly correct and running is what gets you killed — the opposite of what the current text implies. And if the heal is a 12s cast rather than ambient regen, it is a cooldown you can bait and a window anti-heal is timed to.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout only slows you if your back is turned — hold the Flamespitter cone on him and walk through, never away. Bloodlust is a 12s active heal, not regeneration: bait it, then commit while it is down, and land Grievous Wounds before he casts it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json (Mocking Shout: 'Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced'; Bloodlust cd 12, 'He can cast Bloodlust to consume his Fury and heal himself')

audit.whatIsWrong: Spinning Slash is named repeatedly as his gap-closer and disengage but never given a cooldown.
audit.why: It is the most punishable cooldown in the lane — 12s at rank 1 down to 8s at rank 5. Rumble's whole level-3 window is 'trade while his escape is down'.
audit.corrected: Spinning Slash is 12s at rank 1. Once he spins in, he has no way out for twelve seconds — that is the trade window, not the moment he lands.

edits.after: Tryndamere's Undying Rage means your all-in fails completely if you commit when it is up — it is 120s at rank 1, so count it or your Equalizer means nothing.

edits.before: Levels 4–5 are where Tryndamere starts to assert himself. His Mocking Shout W drops your movement speed, letting him out-chase you after a Spinning Slash gap-close, and his crit autos hit hard enough to rip through Scrap Shield before you can Q back. You want to play for chip damage only — never full commit unless Undying Rage is confirmed down. At Level 6 your Equalizer changes the map but not this 1v1: if Tryndamere has Rage available he will just eat the rockets and walk. The most honest play in this window is using Equalizer to win a skirmish elsewhere rather than trying to solo-kill him — roam with it, not at him.
edits.after: Levels 4–5 are where Tryndamere starts to assert himself. Mocking Shout only slows you if your back is turned, so the instinct to run is what kills you here — hold the cone on him and walk through, and the W does nothing but cut attack damage you do not use. His crits still rip through Scrap Shield before you can Q back, so play for chip damage only and never full commit unless Undying Rage is confirmed down. At Level 6 your Equalizer changes the map but not this 1v1: with Rage available he simply eats the rockets and walks away. The honest play in this window is using Equalizer to win a skirmish elsewhere — roam with it, not at him.

edits.before: His crits start hurting and Mocking Shout W keeps him on you after a Spinning Slash — he wins extended fights from here, so take short poke trades and never let Heat lapse to zero in his face.
edits.after: Mocking Shout only slows you if you turn your back, so face him and keep the cone on — he still wins extended fights, so take short poke trades and never let Heat lapse to zero in his face.

edits.before: Full crit Tryndamere heals chip with fury regen and kite-spins through everything you have — your win condition is Equalizer across choke points in teamfights, not any 1v1 with him.
edits.after: Full crit Tryndamere erases chip with a 12-second Bloodlust cast, not regen — bait it, then commit; your win condition is Equalizer across choke points, never a 1v1 with him.

edits.before: This is Tryndamere's lane in the late game. He spin-kites through your Flamespitter cone, crits through your Scrap Shield, and his passive fury regeneration undoes your chip between trades. You cannot 1v1 him at full build if he has even one more item. Your job is to win teamfights through Equalizer — lay it across chokepoints and disengage for your team rather than ever trying to duel him alone. If he is splitpushing, do not match him; instead use the 1v1 pressure he creates to force a teamfight on the other side of the map where your ultimate decides the outcome.
edits.after: This is Tryndamere's lane in the late game. He spin-kites through your Flamespitter cone, crits through your Scrap Shield, and undoes your chip with Bloodlust — a 12-second cast, not regeneration, so anti-heal has to land before he presses it. You cannot 1v1 him at full build if he has even one more item. Your job is to win teamfights through Equalizer — lay it across chokepoints and disengage for your team rather than duelling him. If he splitpushes, do not match him; use the pressure he creates to force a fight across the map where your ultimate decides it.

edits.before: Track Tryndamere's Undying Rage: Unkillable 5s. Kite it out. When it is down — Flame + E-R him.
edits.after: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1 — kite it out. Mocking Shout slows only if you turn your back.

notes: All three packet suspectNames are false positives — "Scrap Shield's", 'Spinning Slashes' and 'His Mocking Shout' are correct names in ordinary English forms. The genuine defects were numeric and mechanical: a '110-second' Undying Rage cooldown that matches no rank (real: 120/100/80), repeated twice; Mocking Shout described as an unconditional slow when it only slows targets with their backs turned; and Bloodlust's heal described as passive fury regeneration when it is a 12s active cast. The Mocking Shout correction reverses the recommended behaviour — face him and hold the cone rather than backing off — so it is worth a second look before applying.
